text:
oliver: heads-up, saw a weird eviction storm on canary-2 this morning. multiple requests hit a shard while warmup was in-flight and we served stale KV-prefixs. not a full corruption but returned older key-cache -> downstream logits drifted for short bursts :grimacing:
sara: ugh. any logs/trace? spike windows?
matt: i pulled the traces. the read-lease TTL was 2s and warmup sometimes takes 3-4s under IO pressure. lease expired -> cache invalidated -> concurrent warmup wrote a new prefix but some workers read old in-memory pointers.
lina: sounds like a classic race: eviction/invalidation racing with streaming hydration. we don't have a generation check on the in-memory prefix objects, just TTL. propose we add a per-shard generation counter in the manifest and attach it to leases. when applying a cache entry, verify gen == current manifest gen.
josh: that would be simple and effective. example header i'm imagining:
```
Lease: { shard: "s-122", gen: 134, issued_at: 8276549980, ttl: 5000 }
Manifest: { shard: "s-122", gen: 135, origin: "registry-az1" }
```
validate that cached.gen >= manifest.gen? we should decide directionality carefully.
karen: careful: comparing >= might mask rollbacks. better: require exact equality or a monotonic check with signed manifests. if manifest.gen < cached.gen -> possible stale manifest (rollback) -> fail-safe fetch entire shard. also add a short backoff on eviction when warmup is in progress so we don't thrash.
oliver: good catch on rollbacks. what about atomic swap semantics for hotfill? can we do a CAS on the shard descriptor so readers either see old OR new, never mixed?
lina: yes, we can publish new descriptor with new gen then atomically swap pointer. readers should read descriptor first then the KV prefix. ordering: read descriptor -> read prefix -> validate prefix.gen == descriptor.gen. if mismatch, retry after a tiny jitter. keeps eligibility deterministic.
matt: implementation note: need to ensure cross-process visibility when using shared memory for KV pointers. on linux, ensure msync ordering or use an atomic pointer in shm that is set last after writes complete.
sara: do we need protocol changes for safetensors/manifest producers? producers should increment gen when uploading new shards and add a small handshake that tells warmup not to evict recently-written generations for N seconds.
josh: +1 to producer-side hints. also telemetry: record (descriptor.gen, prefix.gen) pairs on cache hits so we can catch mismatches in perf dashboards.
karen: ops concern: this will temporarily increase memory usage (we may keep both old+new until swap) — need to model worst-case footprint and add eviction headroom in Dedicated plans. might affect SLA notes.
deploy-bot: canary rollout paused for pool canary-2 due to cache-consistency spike.
oliver: ok next actions: 1) add gen field to manifest + producer contract (lina, josh) 2) implement atomic descriptor swap + validation (matt, sara) 3) producer hint for eviction grace (lina) 4) dashboard telemetry for gen mismatches (josh) 5) SLO cost impact analysis (karen). volunteers? :raised_hand:
sara: i'll take 2 (impl + tests)
matt: i'll pair on atomic swap (2) and handle shm ordering notes
lina: i'll draft the manifest-gen RFC and producer contract
josh: i'll add telemetry + a small prototype in the loader harness
karen: i'll run the footprint/SLA analysis and give numbers by EOD tomorrow
oliver: awesome. i'll open a follow-up thread for the RFC diffs and drop a spike ticket. thanks all :thumbsup:
